newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica shares end mixed, dogged by system problems.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica shares end mixed, dogged by system problems.

text.p: South African gold shares dived on a weak bullion price, which fixed in London at its lowest level in 20 months, shaving over two percent off the index.
Industrial shares retraced earlier losses ending a touch firmer, boosted by futures players in afternoon trade.

But dealers said trade was hampered for most of the day by the Johannesburg Equities Trading system which was initially shut down for three hours in the morning and again at 1310 GMT for the rest of the trading session following response problems.

Industrial shares initially drifted lower on negative sentiment on fears of a correction on Wall Street as it has steamed higher and worries over a slower economic growth after a surprise interest rate hike last week, dealers said.
They said foreigners had kept to the sidelines for most of the day.
The market was seen continuing volatile on Tuesday on a weak bullion price and fears of a correction on Wall Street.
The gold index ended down 39.2 points to 1,621.3 points, pulling the all share index down 35.4 points to 6,691.3. The industrial index was up 2.8 points to 7,954.8 points.
